## Context

The fixture-admission runner (`src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_admission.py`, epic REB-693 / 67aa) scopes out container criteria (G3/G4/decomp-shape) as `container-material-unrecoverable`: the replay corpus (`src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/corpus.py`) persists a review's children as bare ticket-id strings only (`_child_ids`), with no per-child title/description. The live plan-review container finder reads each child's full title/description at review time (`context_assembly.py` fetches every child via `show_ticket`), and G3's coverage-discharge cannot fire on an impoverished roster. A container case rehydrated from the corpus therefore runs the finder over material that is not faithful to the historical review. `material_fingerprint` hashes children by id only (`material_diff.py`), so it cannot detect the loss.

## Approach

Extend the plan-replay corpus sidecar to persist per-child at-review material as `{canonical_id, title, description}`.

Implementation details:

- Extend `_reconstruct_material` (or a small sibling helper used by it) to reconstruct `title` as well as `description`: start from the child's CREATE `data["title"]`, then apply EDIT `fields["title"]` events up to `review_ts` using the same timestamp gating / last-write semantics already used for description.
- Thread the full per-ticket event mapping returned by `_load_ticket_events` into `_build_sidecar_row`; do not try to reconstruct child material from the parent ticket's `by_type` events. For each `_child_ids(reviewed_related_material)` entry, look up the child's own events and reconstruct that child's title/description as of the parent review timestamp.
- Persist both legacy `_child_ids` and the new per-child material field during new corpus capture so old consumers keep working while container replay has faithful inputs.
- Rehydrate container contexts from the persisted child material into the `{ticket_id, title, description}` records consumed by the container finder.
- Treat missing or unrecoverable child material as unrecoverable, not as an empty/degraded roster. That includes legacy rows that predate the new per-child material field and child histories whose CREATE event or title/description cannot be reconstructed at `review_ts`.
- Remove the container scope-out in `fixture_admission.run_admission` only after the rehydration path can supply faithful child material or explicitly withhold the case.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/corpus.py`: reconstruct and persist per-child review-time title/description, and rehydrate the finder context from that material.
- `src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_admission.py`: stop withholding G3/G4/decomp-shape cases solely because they are container criteria once child material is faithful.
- `tests/**` covering synthetic child histories, legacy rows, unrecoverable child material, and container admission dispatch.
- Generated G3/G4/decomp-shape eval spec artifacts only if a live admission run mints changed faithful specs within the existing fixture-admission budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The corpus sidecar row persists per-child `{canonical_id, title, description}` reconstructed at `review_ts`; a unit test over synthetic child histories asserts CREATE title/description and EDIT title/description updates are reflected as of the parent review timestamp.
- [ ] `_build_sidecar_row` receives the full per-ticket event store from `_load_ticket_events` and reconstructs each child from the child's own events, not the parent's events.
- [ ] Rehydrated container cases pass child title/description records to the finder and G3/G4/decomp-shape are no longer withheld as `container-material-unrecoverable` solely because they are container criteria.
- [ ] A child whose at-review material is unrecoverable, and any legacy corpus row missing the new per-child material, withholds that case to drift as unrecoverable rather than calling the finder with an empty/degraded child roster.
- [ ] The existing protection for non-container criteria and rows with no children is unchanged.
- [ ] A live admission run for G3/G4/decomp-shape either mints faithful specs or records a bounded, explicit no-change/unavailable result in the existing fixture-admission ledger. The spend cap is the existing admission ledger cap enforced by `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/ledger.py`; the ledger must show the run stayed within that configured cap.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck`, targeted plan-replay/fixture-admission tests, and `make test` pass. The Gerrit change receives LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1, is submitted, and this ticket closes after the merged commit is reachable from `origin/main`.
